claims.text: Low-temperature, high-alkalinity continuous-solvothermal synthesis promotes controlled multimetal reduction.
The closed-loop synthesis and selection approach produces beneficial post-ageing Cu–Pt electronic coupling.
The proposed approach will improve automotive exhaust-catalyst activity.
The proposed approach will improve automotive exhaust-catalyst durability.
The proposed approach will reduce platinum-group-metal consumption.
Fresh 1 wt% multielement catalyst candidates on La-doped γ-Al2O3 typically contain agglomerates of fine metallic particles.
The intervention fosters post-ageing electronic and atomic reconstruction.
The intervention fosters controlled multimetal nucleation.
Cu–Pt electronic coupling and controlled multimetal nucleation improve adsorption and activation dynamics.
Cu–Pt electronic coupling and controlled multimetal nucleation mitigate detrimental segregation or excessive Pt isolation.
High alkalinity and lower synthesis temperatures support synchronous multimetal reduction.
High alkalinity and lower synthesis temperatures limit phase segregation.
Ageing-induced electronic redistribution causes beneficial Cu–Pt surface rearrangement.
Cu–Pt surface rearrangement weakens overly strong CO binding.
Cu–Pt surface rearrangement enhances redox buffering and oxygen mobility.
Pt coordination with Ni or Fe can hinder adsorption and catalytic activity.
Closed-loop-discovered catalysts will achieve at least a 5 °C lower T50 or at least a 2 percentage-point higher conversion at 350 °C relative to the stated benchmarks.
Closed-loop-discovered catalysts will exhibit enhanced low-temperature and total conversion after ageing.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome defines success as meeting either the 5 °C T50 improvement or the 2 percentage-point conversion improvement, whereas the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis if either threshold is missed. Thus, a catalyst meeting one stated success threshold but not the other would simultaneously satisfy the prediction and trigger rejection.
